main.title: Deathrow
main.subtitle: A disc sport with room for a fight
main.summary: Deathrow is Southend Interactive's Xbox sports game, first released in Europe on 18 October 2002. Its invented sport, Blitz, puts two teams of four into an arena where scoring and fighting are both legitimate routes to victory. Players carry and pass an energised disc before throwing it through the opposition's raised hoop. A team can win on points or by knocking out every opponent. That second possibility changes the meaning of defence: a player away from the disc can still influence the result by removing someone who would otherwise contest it.

cards.heading: A disc sport with room for a fight
cards.text: Deathrow is Southend Interactive's Xbox sports game, first released in Europe on 18 October 2002. Its invented sport, Blitz, puts two teams of four into an arena where scoring and fighting are both legitimate routes to victory. Players carry and pass an energised disc before throwing it through the opposition's raised hoop. A team can win on points or by knocking out every opponent. That second possibility changes the meaning of defence: a player away from the disc can still influence the result by removing someone who would otherwise contest it.

cards.heading: Read the space and the people occupying it
cards.text: Passing opens routes through a defence, while punches, kicks and throws can disrupt the players trying to close them. Fighting consumes health, and an exhausted competitor leaves the match until substitutions become available between rounds. Team members can also hurt one another, so indiscriminate aggression creates its own danger. Credits earned from goals, knockouts and crowd-pleasing play support upgrades and recruitment through the campaign. The player develops a team whose strengths should match the preferred balance between moving the disc quickly and imposing physical control over the arena.

cards.heading: A small studio makes a demanding team game
cards.text: Development began as an online PC project before Southend shifted to Xbox and its graphics capabilities. Local and System Link multiplayer supported contests beyond the campaign, though Xbox Live play was absent. Critics praised the energetic action and the unusual sporting idea, while noting the steep learning curve. Strong reviews did not produce enough sales for a sequel. Deathrow remains distinctive because its violence changes the tactical situation rather than merely decorating the sport: every injured player alters the passing options and defensive pressure available to both teams.

main.title: Mario Party 4
main.subtitle: A new console around the same party table
main.summary: Mario Party 4 is Hudson Soft's first GameCube entry in Nintendo's board-game series, released in North America on 21 October 2002.

cards.heading: A new console around the same party table
cards.text: Mario Party 4 is Hudson Soft's first GameCube entry in Nintendo's board-game series, released in North America on 21 October 2002. Four characters travel through themed boards, gathering coins and competing for Stars. A minigame after each round changes the balance before the next set of dice rolls. The familiar mixture gives a group several ways to influence the result: a useful item, a fortunate board event or a strong performance in a short challenge can each alter what the next turn makes possible.

cards.heading: Change size to change the route
cards.text: Mega and Mini Mushrooms make size part of navigating the board. Growing larger provides extra movement and lets a character take coins from opponents passed along the route. Shrinking restricts the dice but opens small pipes and shortcuts. The choice is therefore tied to the current destination: moving farther is useful only if the route still leads somewhere worth reaching. Shops and other items add further ways to approach a Star or disturb another player's plan, keeping the board's social contest active between minigames.

cards.heading: A short challenge interrupts the board
cards.text: The minigames divide the group into free-for-all, paired or uneven teams, sometimes turning an opponent from the board into a temporary partner. Booksquirm asks players to avoid being crushed by falling pages, while Dungeon Duos makes cooperation essential to moving through an obstacle course. Practice opportunities let a group learn a challenge before its scored attempt. Ichiro Shimakura composed the music. The GameCube debut keeps the gathering readable through bright themed spaces and brief changes of activity, with the next round returning every rivalry to the board.

main.title: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4
main.summary: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4 is a 2002 skateboarding game developed by Neversoft and published by Activision under their Activision O2 label.

cards.text: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4 is a 2002 skateboarding game developed by Neversoft and published by Activision under their Activision O2 label. The game was ported by different developers to various systems. It is the fourth installment in the Tony Hawk's series. The game was released in 2002 for the GameCube, PlayStation, PlayStation 2, Xbox, and Game Boy Advance. In 2003, it was released for Windows and Mac OS X by developer Beenox and publisher Aspyr. In 2004, a Tapwave Zodiac version was released. Another port of the Game Boy Advance version was also released as a launch title for the digiBLAST, a Linux-based handheld console for children released in 2005.
A remake of the game is included as part of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 + 4, released in 2025.

main.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2002
main.summary: The Golden Joystick Awards, with every category winner of the 2002 edition.

cards.heading: The players' awards
cards.text: The Golden Joystick Awards celebrate games through a public vote, bringing players into the choice of each year's winners. The awards began in Britain with the 1983 season and later reached an international audience through online voting. Their changing categories trace the growth of games: home computers and consoles, handhelds, online play, independent studios, performance and music. Alongside the public vote, special honours recognise individual contributions to the industry. Each edition preserves its own category names, so the results also show what players and the awards organisers considered worth celebrating at the time.

main.title: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City
main.summary: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a 2002 action-adventure game developed by Rockstar North and published by Rockstar Games.

cards.heading: Tommy Vercetti enters Vice City
cards.text: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a 2002 action-adventure game developed by Rockstar North and published by Rockstar Games. It is the fourth main game in the Grand Theft Auto series, following 2001's Grand Theft Auto III, and the sixth entry overall. Set in 1986 within the fictional Vice City (based on Miami), the single-player story follows gangster Tommy Vercetti's rise to power after being released from prison and becoming caught up in an ambushed drug deal. While seeking out those responsible, Tommy gradually builds a criminal empire by seizing power from other criminal organisations.

cards.heading: Building a city around a particular decade
cards.text: The game is played from a third-person perspective and its world is navigated on foot or by vehicle. The open world design lets the player freely roam Vice City, consisting of two main islands. The game's plot is based on multiple real-world people and events in Miami such as Cubans, Haitians, and biker gangs, the 1980s crack epidemic, the Mafioso drug lords of Miami, and the dominance of glam metal. The game was also influenced by the films and television of the era, most notably Scarface (1983) and Miami Vice (1984–1990). Much of the development work constituted creating the game world to fit the inspiration and time period; the development team conducted extensive field research in Miami while creating the world. The game was released in October 2002 for the PlayStation 2.

cards.heading: Acclaim, controversy and later versions
cards.text: Vice City received critical acclaim, with praise directed at its music, gameplay, story, and open world design, though it generated controversy over its depiction of violence and racial groups. It received year-end accolades from several gaming publications, and it is considered one of the sixth generation of console gaming's most significant titles and among the best video games ever made. Vice City became the best-selling game of 2002 and one of the best-selling PlayStation 2 games with over 14.2 million copies sold; it has sold over 17.5 million copies overall. It was released for Windows and the Xbox in 2003, followed by enhanced versions and mobile ports in the 2010s and a remastered version in 2021. It was followed by Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas (2004) and a prequel, Vice City Stories (2006).

cards.heading: Building the sound of the eighties
cards.text: The game features 8,000 lines of recorded dialogue, four times the amount in Grand Theft Auto III. It contains over 90 minutes of cutscenes and nine hours of music, with more than 113 songs and commercials. The team enjoyed the challenge of creating the game's soundtrack, particularly in contrast to Grand Theft Auto III's music, which Sam Houser described as "clearly satirical and its own thing". In developing the radio stations, the team wanted to reinforce the game's setting by curating a variety of songs from the 1980s, which required extensive research. The radio stations were published by Epic Records on seven albums—known collectively as Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Official Soundtrack Box Set—alongside the game in October 2002. Vice City contains about three times as much talk radio as Grand Theft Auto III. The developers emphasised the extremity of the callers' personalities, drawing from the experiences of producer and talk show host Lazlow Jones. Dan Houser felt the talk stations gave depth to the game world.

main.title: Spyro: Enter the Dragonfly
main.summary: Recovering scattered dragonflies adds a moving target to Spyro's collecting, while different breaths open another set of obstacles.

cards.heading: The game
cards.text: Spyro: Enter the Dragonfly is a 2002 platform adventure developed by Check Six Studios and Equinoxe Digital Entertainment, first released for PlayStation 2 and then GameCube. Ripto's return scatters the young dragons' dragonflies across the realms. Spyro searches portal-linked worlds to bring them back, adding different breath abilities to his charges, glides and gem collecting.

cards.heading: Catch something that can escape
cards.text: A rescued dragonfly has to be caught with Bubble Breath. Some wait at the end of a task, while others move away as Spyro approaches, making the final capture an action of its own. Charging closes the distance but also makes it easier to overshoot. Slowing down gives more time to aim the bubble, at the risk of letting the target turn away. Collecting becomes a small pursuit, with the Atlas recording which dragonflies still remain in each world.

cards.heading: Choose another breath
cards.text: Fire, ice and electricity give Spyro other ways to deal with enemies and obstacles. Switching breath changes the next action without changing the route beneath his feet: a useful attack in one encounter may leave another problem untouched. Bubble Breath has its own purpose in recovering dragonflies, so it also asks the player to remember which ability is currently selected. Looking at the target and choosing the corresponding breath becomes another step between arriving in an area and clearing its tasks.

cards.heading: Glide, land, look again
cards.text: The familiar glide still turns distance and height into a judgement. Spyro launches from one ledge, holds the crossing, then uses a hover to help reach the far edge. Gems and side tasks encourage the player to look around after landing rather than immediately leave through the next portal. Speedways and vehicle activities change the pace between those searches. Returning to a world can mean following a remaining entry in the Atlas or trying a different kind of challenge within the same landscape.

main.title: Ratchet & Clank
main.summary: Ratchet & Clank is a 2002 third-person shooter platform video game developed by Insomniac Games and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2 in 2002.

cards.heading: Ratchet & Clank
cards.text: Ratchet & Clank is a 2002 third-person shooter platform video game developed by Insomniac Games and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2 in 2002. It is the first installment in the Ratchet & Clank series as well as the first game developed by Insomniac to not be owned by Universal Interactive. It follows a Lombax named Ratchet meeting the robot Clank on his home planet, Veldin. Clank discovers that the villainous Chairman Alonzo Drek of the Blarg race plans to create a new planet for his species, destroying other planets in the process. Clank convinces Ratchet to help him in his mission to secure the assistance of the famous superhero Captain Qwark.

cards.heading: Weapons and gadgets across the Solana Galaxy
cards.text: The game offers a wide range of weapons and gadgets that the player must use to defeat numerous enemies and solve puzzles on a variety of different planets in the fictional Solana Galaxy. The game includes several minigames, such as racing or security hacking, which the player must complete to proceed. The game was very well received by critics, who praised the graphics, gameplay, voice acting, audio, soundtrack, and comedic approach to the story; some criticism was directed at the camera, the characterization (especially towards Ratchet's personality) and the low level of difficulty in early stages. It was followed by Ratchet & Clank: Going Commando (2003).

cards.heading: Remasters bring the trilogy forward
cards.text: A high-definition remaster developed by Idol Minds for the PlayStation 3 was included as part of the Ratchet & Clank Collection in 2012, which consists of remasters of the first three games of the series originally developed for the PlayStation 2. A port of the remaster developed by Mass Media for the PlayStation Vita was released in 2014. An official emulation of the original PlayStation 2 version of the game is set to be re-released digitally for the PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 in the final quarter (Q4) of 2026.

cards.heading: The film and its PlayStation 4 companion
cards.text: In April 2016, an animated film based on the game was released, preceded by a remake for PlayStation 4 based on that work.

main.title: MechAssault
main.subtitle: BattleTech reaches the living room
main.summary: MechAssault is an Xbox action game released in North America on 12 November 2002. Set in the BattleTech universe, it puts the player inside a BattleMech working for the mercenary Wolf's Dragoons. An investigation on the planet Helios becomes a campaign against the invading Word of Blake. Day 1 Studios and FASA Studio built the game around console controls, placing the emphasis on moving and fighting rather than the procedures of a detailed cockpit simulation. The result brings the weight of a walking war machine into a direct action format.

cards.heading: BattleTech reaches the living room
cards.text: MechAssault is an Xbox action game released in North America on 12 November 2002. Set in the BattleTech universe, it puts the player inside a BattleMech working for the mercenary Wolf's Dragoons. An investigation on the planet Helios becomes a campaign against the invading Word of Blake. Day 1 Studios and FASA Studio built the game around console controls, placing the emphasis on moving and fighting rather than the procedures of a detailed cockpit simulation. The result brings the weight of a walking war machine into a direct action format.

cards.heading: Bring the surroundings into the fight
cards.text: A BattleMech carries several weapons, but using them demands attention to heat as well as the target. Movement and the surrounding structures help shape an encounter, giving the player reasons to keep changing position. Different machines offer different combinations of speed, armour and firepower. Choosing one changes the way an open space or a close confrontation can be approached. The campaign introduces that range through a sequence of objectives, allowing the player to learn the strengths of a machine while dealing with the forces occupying Helios.

cards.heading: An early meeting place on Xbox Live
cards.text: MechAssault was among the first games to support Xbox Live. Players could find a quick match, search for particular conditions or host a session and invite friends. Deathmatch and team battles carried the campaign's machines into human competition, while other modes changed the objective or the consequences of defeat. The service helped establish routines that became familiar on later consoles: a friends list, voice communication and a match reached from the same game. A sequel, MechAssault 2: Lone Wolf, followed in 2004, extending this console interpretation of BattleTech.

main.title: Unreal Championship
main.subtitle: An arena shooter arrives with Xbox Live
main.summary: Unreal Championship is Digital Extremes and Epic Games' Xbox arena shooter, released in North America on 12 November 2002. Related to Unreal Tournament 2003, it brought the series' rapid multiplayer competition to a console launching its own online service. Players enter enclosed arenas where movement, weapons and knowledge of the surroundings determine the next encounter. The immediate objective is easy to understand, but staying alive requires constant decisions about where to go and what to collect. Xbox Live made those contests part of the original Xbox's developing online identity.

cards.heading: An arena shooter arrives with Xbox Live
cards.text: Unreal Championship is Digital Extremes and Epic Games' Xbox arena shooter, released in North America on 12 November 2002. Related to Unreal Tournament 2003, it brought the series' rapid multiplayer competition to a console launching its own online service. Players enter enclosed arenas where movement, weapons and knowledge of the surroundings determine the next encounter. The immediate objective is easy to understand, but staying alive requires constant decisions about where to go and what to collect. Xbox Live made those contests part of the original Xbox's developing online identity.

cards.heading: Know what the route can give you
cards.text: An arena's weapons and supplies give movement a purpose beyond escaping the opponent currently in view. Reaching a useful pickup can prepare the next confrontation, while taking a predictable route can expose the player to someone waiting for it. The speed of the game makes those choices recur quickly. A lost encounter becomes information about an approach that failed or a resource that arrived too late. Familiarity gradually turns the arena from a collection of corridors into a set of connected opportunities, each useful only if reached at the right moment.

cards.heading: Console competition becomes something that can be maintained
cards.text: Unreal Championship was an early demonstration of how an established PC multiplayer design could operate through a console online service. It also became notable for receiving a downloadable console patch, showing that the released game could be adjusted after reaching players. Reviews were generally favourable, and it joined the Xbox Platinum Hits range. The original Xbox Live service later closed, ending its official online support. Its historical place belongs to the period when networked console games were becoming ongoing shared spaces, with competition and maintenance continuing beyond the disc in the box.

main.title: Resident Evil Zero
main.summary: Resident Evil Zero (or Resident Evil 0) is a 2002 survival horror game developed and published by Capcom for the GameCube.

cards.text: Resident Evil Zero (or Resident Evil 0) is a 2002 survival horror game developed and published by Capcom for the GameCube. It is a prequel to Resident Evil (2002), following S.T.A.R.S. officer Rebecca Chambers and convict Billy Coen as they explore an abandoned training facility for employees of the pharmaceutical company Umbrella in the outskirts of Raccoon City. The gameplay is similar to other Resident Evil games, but adds the ability to switch between characters to solve puzzles and use unique abilities.

Development for Resident Evil Zero began for the Nintendo 64 in 1998. The partner system was created to take advantage of the short load times possible with the capabilities of the Nintendo 64 Game Pak. The cartridge format also provided limitations, as the storage capacity was significantly less than that of a CD-ROM. The team had to approach the design differently from previous series entries to conserve storage space. Resident Evil Zero was designed to be more difficult than previous Resident Evil games. Inspired by Sweet Home (1989), the team removed the item storage boxes present in earlier games and introduced a new item-dropping feature. Production was switched to the recently unveiled GameCube after development slowed due to memory storage issues. Only the concept and story remained from the original game, which had to be rebuilt.

Resident Evil Zero received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised the graphics and audio for building a haunting atmosphere. Opinions on the new partner and item systems were mixed. Some found the changes were an improvement and added new layers of strategy; others believed the changes were cumbersome or non-innovative. The game's tank controls were criticized as outdated.

The game was ported to the Wii in 2008, and a high-definition remaster was released in January 2016; the rereleases received mixed reviews due to lack of improvements. Resident Evil Zero was commercially successful, having sold over 4 million copies across all platforms.
